gen_risks.description: Construction of the new training center on Príncipe may be delayed due to procurement and weather-related challenges.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt accelerated procurement, include contingency timelines, use modular construction, and monitor weather forecasts closely.
gen_risks.evidence: Construction of a new multi-use technical training center... adjustments will be managed within the project’s procurement plan.

gen_risks.description: Existing training institutions may lack adequate equipment, infrastructure, and staff to deliver quality market‑aligned training.
gen_risks.mitigation: Upgrade equipment, fund instructor upskilling, provide performance‑based compensation, and monitor capacity against a standardized checklist.
gen_risks.evidence: Capacity remains constrained... outdated equipment, limited infrastructure, staffing gaps.

gen_risks.description: The labor market information system and Employability Portal may not become fully operational, limiting job matching.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign dedicated IT staff, pilot test modules, ensure integration with USR and social security databases, and set clear rollout milestones.
gen_risks.evidence: Employment Observatory never fully operationalized; digital Employability Portal never launched.

gen_risks.description: Beneficiary selection could exclude the most vulnerable or be captured by elites, reducing equity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use USR data for transparent criteria, conduct independent verification, and strengthen the grievance redress mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: Risks of exclusion... if project benefits are not equitably distributed, elite capture.

gen_risks.description: Risk of sexual exploitation, abuse or harassment (SEA/SH) for young women participating in training and internships.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce GBV/SEA policies, provide safe training locations, child‑care support, and a confidential reporting system.
gen_risks.evidence: Risk of sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and sexual harassment (SH), particularly for young women.

gen_risks.description: Delays and weaknesses in financial management could impede timely payments to beneficiaries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint an experienced accountant, customize the accounting system, conduct regular internal audits, and provide staff capacity building.
gen_risks.evidence: FM risks identified include delays in recording financial transactions and generating financial reports.

gen_risks.description: Procurement processes may stall due to insufficient coordination between AFAP and line ministries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create a joint procurement task force, define clear TORs and timelines, and conduct coordination workshops.
gen_risks.evidence: Key factor for good procurement performance will be ability of AFAP and the MLSSS to work in close collaboration.

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related hazards (floods, storms) could disrupt training delivery and construction activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement climate‑resilient designs, install backup generators, schedule activities flexibly, and activate the CERC if needed.
gen_risks.evidence: STP vulnerable to coastal floods, severe storms... may cause disruptions in service delivery.

gen_risks.description: Activation of the Contingent Emergency Response Component may be delayed or lack sufficient funds.
gen_risks.mitigation: Finalize the CERC manual before effectiveness, pre‑identify trigger criteria, and retain a reserve fund for rapid use.
gen_risks.evidence: CERC manual to be prepared after project effectiveness; activation follows procedures.

gen_risks.description: Training outputs may not match evolving private‑sector demand, reducing employment outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain active Workforce Development Committees, use real‑time labor market data to adjust curricula, and conduct quarterly employer surveys.
gen_risks.evidence: Employers will be engaged in defining priority skills... to review training offerings.

gen_risks.description: Labor‑mobility pathways could be hindered by policy changes in destination countries such as Portugal.
gen_risks.mitigation: Diversify destination partnerships, monitor migration policies, and embed flexible MOUs covering multiple jurisdictions.
gen_risks.evidence: Labor mobility approach depends on partnerships with overseas employers; risk of policy changes.

gen_risks.description: The Project Implementation Unit may lack sufficient skilled staff, leading to fragmented execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit two senior specialists and two assistants as planned, provide onboarding training, and establish clear reporting lines.
gen_risks.evidence: PIU will be reinforced with additional consultants; single PIU Coordinator will oversee implementation.

gen_risks.description: Corruption or fraud in grant and stipend disbursements could undermine project credibility.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement electronic payments, conduct independent audits, publish beneficiary lists, and enforce the grievance redress mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: Guidelines on Preventing and Combating Fraud and Corruption in Projects will be applied.

gen_risks.description: Scholarship and grant amounts may be insufficient to cover transport and living costs, causing drop‑outs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Periodically review cost surveys, adjust stipend levels, and provide additional transport vouchers where needed.
gen_risks.evidence: Scholarships up to US$1,000; may not fully cover transportation, accommodation.

gen_risks.description: The new training center may fail to achieve EDGE certification, increasing operational carbon emissions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage certified green‑design consultants, monitor compliance during construction, and install energy‑efficient systems.
gen_risks.evidence: Aim to meet at least Level 1 of IFC’s EDGE certification.

gen_risks.description: Delay in completing the impact evaluation could limit learning and evidence generation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Contract the evaluation firm early, set interim deliverables, and allocate dedicated budget for timely completion.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 3 will finance an impact evaluation; evaluation to be completed end of project.

gen_risks.description: High turnover of newly hired instructors may erode training quality over time.
gen_risks.mitigation: Offer competitive contracts, continuous professional development, and retention bonuses tied to performance.
gen_risks.evidence: Need to contract additional instructors; financing instructor upskilling, retraining.

gen_risks.description: External economic shocks (fuel price volatility, pandemic resurgence) could reduce private‑sector hiring capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Diversify sector focus, include flexible internship placements, and build resilience through climate‑smart skill training.
gen_risks.evidence: STP’s economy affected by COVID‑19, fuel and food import cost volatility.

gt_risks.description: Frequent government changes and the cross-ministerial nature of the jobs agenda can shift policy direction, counterpart arrangements, and implementation momentum; further changes may follow the mid-2026 legislative/parliamentary elections. Success depends on sustained coordination across labor, education, tourism, agriculture, and finance ministries plus private-sector engagement.
gt_risks.mitigation: Anchor the project within MLSSS (core employment-promotion mandate); strengthen technical ownership at directorate level rather than relying on political leadership; establish a formal coordination committee and a unified PIU; continue policy dialogue with Government during implementation.

gt_risks.description: STP's fragile growth outlook, narrow fiscal space, and dependence on external financing leave it highly vulnerable to external shocks (energy/food price swings, donor-disbursement delays, climate events), which may weaken labor demand, reduce firms' absorption capacity, and constrain the Government's ability to sustain recurrent-cost interventions (training, stipends, employment services).
gt_risks.mitigation: Prioritize low-cost, scalable interventions; combine supply-side investments with direct job-creation support; target sectors with growth potential and external demand linkages (incl. labor mobility); coordinate with other World Bank macro-fiscal/energy/private-sector engagements in STP.

gt_risks.description: Limited experience of MLSSS and DTEFP in delivering complex labor-market interventions at scale; fragmented institutional landscape; multiple implementation partners; nascent capacity in labor-market analytics, employment intermediation, and cross-sectoral coordination; sustainability risk if new systems/programs are not institutionalized within government structures and budgets.
gt_risks.mitigation: Leverage existing institutions/mechanisms rather than parallel structures (existing MLSSS PIU, coordination committee, AFAP for fiduciary/safeguards); finance targeted TA and staffing; invest in durable institutional assets (labor-market information system, employability portal, strengthened training institutions, formalized service-provider arrangements); use the learning agenda and impact evaluation to identify cost-effective interventions for scale-up.

gt_risks.description: Complex procurement in a small-island context: residual FM risk is moderate but residual procurement risk is substantial, driven by the complexity of civil works in a remote island context, the large number of technical-assistance contracts, and the multiplicity of projects already handled by AFAP.
gt_risks.mitigation: Agree ToRs and technical specifications between AFAP and the World Bank before initiating any procurement (prior and post-review); reinforce AFAP procurement and contract-management capacity incl. specialized support for civil-works supervision; embed dedicated fiduciary controls for the grants/stipends payment mechanism in the Project Operations Manual; continue and adapt the risk assessment during implementation.
